name: Luxembourg National Division
content:
The Luxembourg National Division, also known as the BGL Ligue for sponsorship reasons, is the top-tier football league in Luxembourg. Founded in 1910, it represents the highest level of the country’s football pyramid and is organized under UEFA. The league currently features 16 teams, with clubs competing not only for the national title but also for qualification to European competitions such as the UEFA Champions League and UEFA Conference League.

The competition has a long history, having been played almost continuously since its creation, with interruptions only during certain early years and World War II, as well as the abandoned 2019–20 season due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Over time, the league has undergone several name changes, reflecting its evolution, before adopting the current “National Division” name in 1957. Historically, Jeunesse Esch is the most successful club, holding the record for the most titles.

Today, the league operates on a seasonal basis, typically running from summer to late spring. Teams compete in a round-robin format, with the lowest-ranked clubs relegated to the Division of Honour and top teams earning spots in European competitions. The Luxembourg National Division remains semi-professional but plays a key role in the development of football in the country and its representation on the international stage.

name: Luxembourg Cup
content:
The Luxembourg Cup is the main national knockout football competition in Luxembourg. First held in 1922, it has become one of the country’s most important domestic tournaments, organized alongside the league system by the Luxembourg Football Federation. The competition features a large number of teams from different divisions, giving smaller clubs the opportunity to compete against top-tier sides in a single-elimination format.

The tournament has been played almost every year since its creation, with only a few interruptions during World War II and more recently due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Matches are played in knockout rounds, culminating in a final typically held at the Stade de Luxembourg. The winner of the competition earns qualification to European competitions, currently the UEFA Europa Conference League qualifying rounds.

Historically, the Luxembourg Cup has seen dominance from several clubs, with Red Boys Differdange being the most successful team in its history. In modern seasons, clubs like Differdange 03 and F91 Dudelange have been among the prominent competitors. Despite being a relatively small football nation, the cup remains a key part of Luxembourg’s football culture and provides an important pathway for clubs to gain international exposure.
